absent: Early portion of modern probe mapping common, interrupt status and notify areas and its success path beyond the device mapping tail.
Bodies of admin activation, cleanup, transport features and common size checks named as extra sids in the final header.
Legacy queue discovery, deletion, vector synchronization, bus naming and affinity handling referenced by the operations table.
Power management operations, PCI identifier table and probe routine referenced by the PCI driver structure.
Admin command execution path, buffer allocation and error handling beyond list initialization and parts enablement.
Exact failure codes for modern mapping and reset forwarding beyond the warning behavior shown.
Device specific configuration layout and queue notification mechanics beyond byte wise legacy access and feature selection.

findings.text: Per queue bookkeeping pairs a core transport queue handle with list membership for dispatch grouping and a stored interrupt vector number for routing.
Admin queue state bundles its queue helper with a dedicated lock for serialization, negotiated command and capability masks, an object limit plus identifier allocator, a short name and a queue index.

PCI transport device embeds a generic virtio device and PCI device pointer, with a union selecting legacy or modern register state plus a flag recording the active side. A mapped interrupt status area supports read and clear, while two queue lists and an array sized by the common configuration count enable dispatch.

Same transport device carries interrupt management state including enable indicators, affinity masks, name storage, vector counts and a per queue vector indicator. It also stores callbacks for queue setup and teardown plus configuration vector assignment and admin queue location lookup.
Configuration interrupt role has value zero and queue interrupt role has value one, fixing their positions in vector allocation.
Legacy device configuration area starts at byte twenty without MSI-X and at byte twenty four with MSI-X, reflecting the larger header when that mode is enabled.
Admin queue scatter gather limit is four entries, bounding how many segments an admin command may describe.

Admin command allowlist combines a legacy group covering common and device configuration access plus notify information with a device parts group covering capability query and install, resource object lifecycle, and parts metadata and mode operations. One build variant merges both groups while another keeps only the device parts group.

Build time checks require symbolic register offsets for capability header fields, notify multiplier, and the full common configuration set including feature selectors, status, generation, queue addressing and extended modern fields to equal the corresponding structure member offsets.
Legacy transport exposes only low thirty two host feature bits and accepts only low thirty two guest bits, with finalization enforcing that no higher bit is set.

Modern capability discovery walks vendor PCI capabilities, discards entries with out of range BAR numbers, and selects the matching type whose BAR has nonzero length and acceptable resource flags, recording the BAR in an output mask.

Admin queue location is reported only when the admin queue feature is negotiated, otherwise count stays zero. When present the stored count must be nonzero or lookup fails, with values sourced from the modern common area.

Admin queue lock serializes completion processing against concurrent use. Completion handling holds it with interrupts saved across callback suppression, buffer reclamation with signaling, and re enable retry until the queue stays enabled.

Modern mapping teardown unwinds in reverse order with optional device and notify areas before interrupt status and common areas, finishing with release of claimed BARs. Normal removal follows the same conditional unmapping and release without error propagation.

PCI removal retains a device reference, flags breakage on surprise absence, disables virtual functions, unregisters the virtio device, dispatches to legacy or modern teardown by transport mode, then disables the PCI device and drops the reference.

Error recovery prepare forwards to virtio preparation and then disables the PCI device when enabled, warning only on unexpected failures. Completion re enables and masters the PCI device when disabled, forwards to virtio completion, and warns on unexpected failures.

Admin completion reclaims buffers until empty, mapping short device writes to zero result payload and longer writes to length beyond the status header, completing each command and repeating the suppress drain enable cycle until callbacks remain enabled.

Admin initialization queries the supported list, masks it to the local allowlist, installs the selection and records the outcome. Device parts enablement then reads capabilities, clamps get and set object limits to their minimum, installs them and initializes identifier allocation with the clamped limit.
PCI driver registers with probe and remove callbacks, optional power management, virtual function configuration, and error recovery handlers for reset prepare and completion.

Legacy transport publishes configuration operations covering byte access, status access and reset, queue discovery and deletion with callback synchronization, feature query and finalization, bus naming and queue affinity.
Modern removal entry forwards from the wrapper holding the full transport device to the low level routine operating only on modern state.
Modern helpers shared across files provide extended feature collection through iterated selector reads, admin queue count and index retrieval, completion draining, and mapping teardown.
Legacy helpers shared across files provide host and guest feature register access, status register access, and configuration vector assignment with read back verification.

Setting legacy status to zero is forbidden except through reset, and finalization aborts if features exceed thirty two bits. Absent hardware must be flagged broken before unregister to abort upper layers. Virtual function setup must reject when driver not ready, when the required feature is missing, or when functions are already assigned.

Legacy reset uses zero status followed by a status read to flush posted writes including interrupts, plus vector synchronization to drain pending callbacks. Configuration vector assignment likewise needs a read back to confirm resources and flush the write.
Legacy configuration reads and writes proceed one byte at a time from a base combining the mapped area, the interrupt mode dependent header size, and the caller offset.
Modern compilation defines guards that disable legacy ring and PCI paths, constraining the build to modern only behavior.

Extended feature collection clears the destination then iterates over thirty two bit windows, selecting each window before reading its value and merging it into the appropriate half of each sixty four bit element.
